## Installing Databricks

#### No Simba Spark ODBC Driver

When you download Simba Spark it doesn't necessarily download the data driver, to do this raise an I.T. ticket explaining that you have installed "Simba Spark" but the driver is missing, they will download it from the internet.

#### Spark

##### Virtual environments

Sometimes R will tell you to install pysparklyr and rerun, then when doing that it sets up a Python venv r-sparklyr-databricks-15.4 on your Onedrive, then it tries to install databricks-connect in the venv but exits with an error 
distutils.errors.DistutilsPlatformError: Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 or greater is required. Get it with "Microsoft C++ Build Tools": https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/

First step: how to get pysparklyr to not install its new virtual environment on Onedrive.  You can specify the default folder for new virtual environments in the .Renvironfile by using the variable WORKON_HOME (e.g. WORKON_HOME = "C:/users/myusername" ) So first edit the file to do that, using usethis::edit_r_environ() (unless you want to use OneDrive, but it looks likely to induce lots of unnecessary syncing), and restart R.
 
Next step: follow the instructions at Set up Databricks personal compute cluster with RStudio – Analysts’ Guide and get to the point of connecting with:
```r
#| sc <- spark_connect(
#|  cluster_id = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_CLUSTER_PATH"),
#|  method = "databricks_connect",
#|)
```
 
Install pysparklyr if it tells you to do that and try again.  Eventually you will probably get a message saying it needs to install a new virtual environment with databricks-connect, and it will now make this in the new folder you specified in WORKON_HOME.  If that goes without a hitch, then great, you're done.
 
But if the installation fails with an error about C++ libraries, you can just install in binary mode yourself.  Go (in Windows explorer) to the Scripts subfolder in the new virtual environment folder it made (probably something like C:\\Users\\myusername\\r-sparklyr-databricks-15.4\\Scripts).  Right-click in the files pane and do "Open in terminal" which will open up Powershell, and in Powershell do .\\python -m pip install databricks-connect.  That should work to install, after which the spark-connect command should now work in R.

:::

## Connecting to Databricks

#### Account removed or gone inactive

Go to the [CIP request form](https://dfe.service-now.com/mydfe?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=51b0b9c5db1ff7809402e1aa4b96197d&referrer=recent_items)

Click: Request type  = "Select Azure Portal and DevOps User Account Request"

If you have never requested an account before click add details and fill out the form.

Otherwise click modify and explain that the account has gone dormant.

#### Personal Access Tokens

You can find guidance on personal access tokens in the [Analysts' Guide](https://dfe-analytical-services.github.io/analysts-guide/ADA/databricks_rstudio_personal_cluster.html#setting-up-the-odbc-driver) and in the [Databricks' guidance](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/api-access-permissions).

1. Find settings button:
![Settings button](/images/ADA/databricks_common_questions/pat_token_1.png)

2. Navigate to settings:
![Workspace swapping between workspaces](/images/ADA/databricks_common_questions/pat_token_2.png)

3. Click developer:
![Workspace swapping between workspaces](/images/ADA/databricks_common_questions/pat_token_3.png)

4. Set-up token:
![Workspace swapping between workspaces](/images/ADA/databricks_common_questions/pat_token_4.png)

Make sure that the personal access token has the "API scope" to do what you want.

The PAT token expiring is commonly the cause for the following error:

Error in `DBI::dbConnect()`:
! ODBC failed with error 28000 from \[Simba\]\[ThriftExtension\].
✖  (8) Authentication/authorization error occurred. Error details: Bad status with no error message: Unauthorized/Forbidden

Other reasons for this error could be either that you do not currently have permission to do what you want with the Catalog, or sometimes a typo in the catalog, databricks host, or warehouse id, guidance can be found in the (Analysts' Guide Databricks connection guidance)[https://dfe-analytical-services.github.io/analysts-guide/ADA/databricks_rstudio_sql_warehouse.html#establishing-an-rstudio-connection-using-environment-variables].

#### PowerBI connection issue

Make sure you are on an up-to-date version of PowerBI or it can struggle to connect.
:::

#### Temporary tables
Temporary tables do not work for Databricks runtimes before 18.1, Databricks [temporary table guidance](https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/en/tables/temporary-tables)

#### Tables vs Volumes

It is common to confuse volumes and tables, you can find guidance on the differences in the 
[Databricks' guidance: volumes](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/volumes/), importantly Volumes are more "blobby" storage so SQL works for reading tables but not for accessing volumes, which you have to do through a slightly different path [Databricks' guidance: volume paths](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/volumes/#path-for-accessing-files-in-a-volume)

#### Using R in notebooks

Your administrator has only allowed sql and python and scala commands on this cluster. This execution contained at least one disallowed language.

#### Retriable errors

Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:3648: HY000 

\[Databricks\]\[Hardy\] (35) Error from server: error code: '0' error message: '\[Databricks\]\[Hardy\] (134) File d6217fa8-e93e-49f6-9a7c-25a12d523025: A retriable error occurred while attempting to download a result file from the cloud store but the retry limit had been exceeded. Error Detail: File d6217fa8-e93e-49f6-9a7c-25a12d523025: An error had occurred while attempting to download the result file.The error is: Could not connect to server. Since the connection has been configured to consider all result file download as retriable errors, we will attempt to retry the download.'. 


The way to fix this error is to set MaxErrorRetry = 0, often setting native query and enabling query result downloads helps.

```r
#|con <- DBI::dbConnect( 
#|
#| odbc::databricks(), 
#| 
#| httpPath = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_CLUSTER_PATH"), 
#|
#| useNativeQuery = FALSE, 
#|
#| EnableQueryResultDownload=TRUE, 
#|
#| MaxErrorRetry=0 
#|
#|) 
```

#### Splink

Some data manipulation with PySpark dataframes don't work, for example you may encounter difficulty using Splink, here is an example of how to get around that using PySpark:
[Splint in PySpark](https://moj-analytical-services.github.io/splink/demos/examples/spark/deduplicate_1k_synthetic.html).


#### Using packages requiring system packages

If you want to use a package that requires system packages, we recommend doing using a notebook and following the [Databricks' guidance on using libraries in r](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/libraries/notebooks-r-libraries).

In general you might want to either convert the PySpark dataframe to a more manageable object:
[Pandas](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/pandas/pyspark-pandas-conversion)
In spark and R you can use the collect() function.

#### I hate Mondays

You can't change the starting day of the week away from Sunday.

##### Package issues

Sometimes Spark updates its packages causing our pipelines to break, there's not much to be done in this case but to roll back the version.

#### Timezones

You can change timezones following this guidance: [Databricks timezones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/databricks/sql/language-manual/parameters/timezone).

#### Pushing up csv's

Special characters in CSV files can cause an issue, if so saving the csv file in UTF-8 encoding (Databricks uses this) should solve the issue.

#### Memory issues

Large dataframes can cause issues with Spark, to get around this you can:

1. use rm() and gc() to clear up as much memory as you can, removing objects you no longer need
2. use a double-size cluster (you can set which cluster type if you're using a personal cluster)
3. use smaller objects (e.g. not copying all columns of a data table if you don't need them all, or selecting a subset before you collect)

:::

## SQL

#### Can't write table to Databricks when you can connect

We recommend using the dfer package and the write_df_to_delta function.

There are a few different kinds of errors that might prevent a table from writing to a database.

##### NAN error

If your table contains NANs, Databricks won't know how to process this.

#### Old code not working

##### Cases

SQL in Databricks is case sensitive, whereas mySQL is not, consider using upper / lower to test.

##### Spaces

SQL in Databricks doesn't automatically trim spaces.

#### Dynamic SQl

Here we can find some guidance on using [Dynamic SQL](https://www.w3tutorials.net/blog/assign-a-variable-a-dynamic-value-in-sql-in-databricks-spark/)

:::
